# RiskFusion — final report

*Numbers come from `reports/evaluation/*.json` (generated by `make pipeline`) and `docs/MODEL_CARD.md`.*

## 1. Summary

RiskFusion combines signals from video, audio and browser activity into a calibrated risk score that orders
online-exam sessions for **human review**. It was built end to end.

**What was built:**
- Consented mock-session recording.
- Pretrained detectors on real recordings.
- A 5,000-session simulator, a versioned feature store, a fusion model with calibration and explanations.
- Fairness and robustness evaluation, a scoring API, reviewer reports, a review queue and drift monitoring.

**Results on the sealed holdout (opened twice, as required):**

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| PR-AUC | 0.835 (95% CI 0.73–0.92) |
| Rule baseline PR-AUC | 0.343 |
| Recall at the operating point | 84% |
| Calibration error (ECE) | 0.016 |
| Missing-channel test | no increase in any score, guaranteed by construction |

**Not achieved:**
- The FPR-disparity target (< 1.3) is not met for every condition. The worst case is candidates with a
  **head covering (9.1% vs 4.7% clean sessions sent to review)**.
- The holdout FPR of 5.3% exceeds the 3% budget set on calibration data.
- All results are on **simulated** data. The consented mock corpus (FR-2, target 60 sessions) has not been
  recorded yet, so FR-3 and FR-6 exist as working code but have not been run on real volunteers.

## 2. What was built (by phase)

| Phase | Delivered |
|---|---|
| 0 | Pinned environment; event.v1 / risk_assessment.v1 contracts with a single registry; SRS audit (26 findings) |
| 1 | Seeded simulator; consent and mock recording (webcam, telemetry, script cues); DR-4 label store; splits with a guarded sealed holdout |
| 2 | Detectors on recordings: SCRFD face, ArcFace identity, head pose, YOLOX objects/persons, audio VAD + speaker heuristic; explicit UNKNOWN for liveness and pose (no licensed models); FR-6/FR-3 measurement code |
| 3 | 1-second grid with gaps, 30 s out-of-order window, 273 features (windows, baseline normalisation, interactions), ROCKET temporal features; Parquet feature store with schema hash |
| 4 | Rule baseline, LightGBM with imbalance handling, temporal model, Platt calibration, capacity-based tiers, experiment log, holdout access 1 |
| 5 | TreeSHAP per prediction, plain-language reasons, time-bounded flags (84% IoU ≥ 0.5), global importance and partial dependence, ablations |
| 6 | Slice metrics with bootstrap CIs, FPR disparity, mitigation, missing-channel guarantee, +50% noise test, cost analysis, reviewer verdicts |
| 7 | `POST /score` (p95 342 ms for 87 min), `/model-info`, batch CLI, HTML reviewer report, drift monitor, model card, `make pipeline`, holdout access 2 |

## 3. Key decisions and findings

**Simulator v1 was too easy.** The first model reached validation PR-AUC 1.0. Every violation was long and loud, and
every false alarm was a 2–3 second blip. A perfect score on a simulator measures the simulator, not the model.

Version 1.1 added realistic hard cases:
- **Persistent confounders:** a phone on the desk, background talk, writing on permitted scratch paper,
  notifications, identity drift in poor light.
- **Evasive violations (35% of positives):** a phone held below the camera, whispering, a second monitor.

v1 remains exactly reproducible (same content hash) for comparison.

**Missing data must never count against a candidate.** Imputation alone does not guarantee this: the first attempt
raised 31% of scores when the environment channel was dropped. The deployed model constrains every feature to be
monotone and imputes missing channels at the risk-lowering end, so `score(channel missing) ≤ score(full)` for every
session by construction. Cost: validation PR-AUC fell from 0.941 (unconstrained) to 0.883. We consider that the
right trade.

**Calibration choice.** Isotonic calibration created ties that scrambled the review order. Platt scaling keeps the
ranking and was within 0.005 ECE, so it is used.

**Ablations (validation PR-AUC):**
- Identity (0.746) and screen telemetry (0.756) are the most important channels.
- Windowed features beat whole-session summaries (0.829 alone).
- A regularised logistic regression is competitive (0.890); the tree model was kept because it supports exact
  per-prediction SHAP and the monotone guarantee.

## 4. Harms of automated proctoring (ETH-5)

Automated proctoring has a documented record of harm, and a system like this can reproduce it.

**False accusation.** Even at our operating point, about 5 in 100 clean sessions on the holdout are sent to a human.
At the scale of a university exam period that is thousands of honest students whose behaviour is examined. A
review is not neutral. Being flagged causes stress and can bias the reviewer towards finding something.

Our mitigations:
- The output is a recommendation with reasons and uncertainty, never a verdict.
- Reports state explicitly that the score can be wrong and why.
- Clean sessions show no flags.
- The tier thresholds are set from reviewer capacity, not from F1.

None of this removes the harm; it only bounds it.

**Disparate impact.** Error rates depend on recording conditions that correlate with who students are and what they
can afford:
- Lighting, webcam quality, room noise and connection stability track income and housing.
- A head covering can indicate religion.

On the holdout, head-covered candidates were sent to review almost twice as often (9.1% vs 4.7%), and unstable
connections raised FPR from 4.7% to 7.2%. Slices are small, so the estimates are uncertain. The direction, however,
matches known failures of face-analysis systems. The mitigation we tried (reweighting) did not fix it. Any
deployment must monitor slice FPRs continuously (the drift monitor does this) and must not apply one threshold to
everyone without checking.

**Surveillance and privacy.** The system records faces, voices and browser behaviour in private homes.

Our mitigations:
- Explicit consent for every participant and helper, with withdrawal that deletes data.
- Demographics stored separately and never used as model inputs.
- No gender or age inference: the pretrained gender/age model is deliberately never loaded.
- Paste content and keystrokes are never recorded, only counts and lengths.
- Retention dates, and deletion of raw media at project end.

**Chilling and accessibility.** Students who look away to think, read aloud, have tics, use assistive technology or
share a room are more likely to be flagged. Per-candidate baseline normalisation reduces this only for continuous
behaviour.

**Automation bias.** Reviewers may defer to a high score. Reports lead with the uncertainty and the evidence, and
the reviewer's verdict is stored separately so the overturn rate can be tracked.

**Requirements for any real use:**
- Human review of every recommendation, and a way for students to see and contest what was flagged.
- Published error rates by condition.
- Alternative arrangements for students who cannot provide a quiet, well-lit room.
- An independent audit on real data before any pilot.

## 5. Limitations

- Trained and evaluated only on simulated data whose detector error rates are estimates.
- The consented mock corpus is not yet recorded, so FR-3 and FR-6 have not run on real volunteers.
- Weak components: a heuristic speaker detector, no liveness model, a head-pose proxy for gaze.
- No authentication (local research prototype); the Docker files have not been built in the development environment.

## 6. Reproduction

`make pipeline` regenerates the data, features, models, evaluation and model card from a fixed seed. See the README.
The sealed holdout access log is committed in `data/splits/sim-v1.1-s20260923-n5000/HOLDOUT_ACCESS_LOG.jsonl`;
both permitted accesses are used, and a third is refused.
